bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a decision or approval record is uniquely designated, versioned as expressions and manifestations, typed, and bounded in subject matter and applicability.
bundles.rationale: An agent cannot cite, deduplicate, supersede or retrieve a decision without a stable identity separated from its versions, and cannot apply the right rules without knowing the decision type and its scope of effect. ECLI proves that decision identity is a governed concern in its own right, and Akoma Ntoso proves that the decision as a work differs from its language and format versions.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: Identifier assignment for the decision act and its record, and the versioned expression structure that keeps corrections and translations distinct from the abstract decision.

findings.name: Decision and record identifier assignment
findings.description: The identifier that designates the decision, the authority that mints it, and the separation between the identifier of the decision act, the identifier of the record and any governed global identifier such as an ECLI.

findings.name: Version, expression and manifestation identity
findings.description: How successive language versions, corrected texts, consolidated texts and published formats of the same decision are distinguished without fragmenting its identity.

findings.name: Title, language and alternative names
findings.description: A short noun-phrase title representing the problem and chosen solution, plus language and any alternative citations. DCMI title and alternative apply; Nygard and MADR require a short representative heading.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Title and language are intrinsic descriptive metadata of the record, not a standalone artefact.

layers.name: Classification and subject matter
layers.description: The type of decision or approval, its binding character, and the subject matter, jurisdiction and population to which it applies.

findings.name: Decision type and binding character
findings.description: Classification of the record along the axes that change how it must be handled: decision family, binding versus advisory, interim versus final, and positive versus negative outcome.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a set of coded attributes of the decision record itself. It produces no separate deliverable object; the controlled vocabularies it draws on are governed by the Dimension's registry links rather than by an artifact of this finding.

findings.name: Subject matter and scope of application
findings.description: What the decision is about and how far its effect reaches — addressees only or a general class, which territory or jurisdiction, and which organisational or asset scope.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and scope are inline descriptive attributes and references to externally governed classification schemes and jurisdiction registers. Producing a separate artifact would duplicate those registers, which belong to sibling classification models.

bundles.name: Substance and reasoning
bundles.description: The decided question, the outcome and any attached conditions or obligations, together with the reasons, alternatives considered and evidence that support the outcome.
bundles.rationale: Substance and reasons are the part of a decision record that authorities most often make mandatory: 5 U.S.C. §557(c) requires findings, conclusions and reasons on all material issues, Charter Article 41(2)(c) imposes a duty to give reasons, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 requires rationale that covers alternatives not chosen. Outcome vocabularies and the obligation/advice split are given normative shape by XACML.

layers.name: Decision substance
layers.description: The question put, the disposition reached, and the conditions, obligations and implementation duties attached to it.

findings.name: Question put for decision
findings.description: The precise question, proposal, motion or request the decision resolves, including how it was framed and by whom it was brought.

findings.name: Outcome and disposition
findings.description: The operative determination: the outcome value, the order or relief granted or refused, and any non-outcome such as deferral, withdrawal or inability to decide.

findings.name: Conditions, obligations, advice and implementation duties
findings.description: What must happen for the decision to take or keep effect, what the decision obliges parties to do, what is merely advisory, and which implementation and enforcement duties follow.

layers.name: Reasoning and evidence
layers.description: The stated reasons, the alternatives weighed and rejected, and the evidence and findings of fact on which the outcome rests.

findings.name: Statement of reasons
findings.description: The reasoning that justifies the outcome, whether giving reasons is legally required for this decision, and whether the reasons form part of the operative instrument or a separate document.

findings.name: Options considered and rejected
findings.description: The alternatives evaluated, the criteria and weights applied, and the recorded justification for rejecting each alternative not chosen.

findings.name: Evidence relied upon and findings of fact
findings.description: The inputs the decision-maker used, the facts found from them, submissions received, and any communications that a rule requires to be placed on the record.

findings.name: Completeness of rulings and confirmation of implementation
findings.description: APA requires the record to show the ruling on each finding, conclusion or exception. MADR confirmation describes how implementation or compliance will be checked. Completeness is a quality property of the decision record; implementation evidence may live in sibling operational models.

bundles.name: Authority, approval and attestation
bundles.description: The competence under which the decision was taken, delegation and limits on it, the participation and voting that produced it, declared conflicts, and the evidence that fixes and attributes the record.
bundles.rationale: A decision that exceeds the decider's competence is voidable, so authority is not metadata but a validity condition. Delaware §141 supplies primary rules on quorum, committee limits, remote presence and action without a meeting; 5 U.S.C. §557 separates presiding, recommending and deciding roles; PROV-O supplies the qualified association and delegation pattern; RFC 3161 supplies third-party time attestation.

layers.name: Mandate and competence
layers.description: The source of power to decide, and the delegation instruments and thresholds that bound it.

findings.name: Decision authority and legal basis
findings.description: Which body or role held competence to take this decision, the instrument conferring that competence, and the rules of composition it had to satisfy.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and approval limits
findings.description: Where the decision was taken under delegated power, the delegation chain, its thresholds and exclusions, and its validity at the decision time.

layers.name: Approval acts, participation and objections
layers.description: The individual acts of approval, participation, voting, dissent and recusal that constitute or evidence the decision.

findings.name: Participation, quorum and vote result
findings.description: Who took part and how, whether quorum was met, how votes or consents were counted, and how decisions taken without a meeting are represented.

findings.name: Dissent, recusal and conflicts of interest
findings.description: Recorded disagreement with the outcome, withdrawals from participation on interest grounds, and declared conflicts affecting the decision's soundness.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Dissents, recusals and conflict declarations are participation events attached to the decision and are normally captured inline in the decision record or in the meeting minutes owned by WM-ACT-025. Where a dissent is issued as a standalone opinion document it is carried as an additional expression under f02 rather than as an artifact unique to this finding.

layers.name: Attestation and record integrity
layers.description: The evidence that fixes the record's content and attributes it to its signatories, and the point at which it becomes unalterable.

findings.name: Signature, seal, time-stamp and integrity evidence
findings.description: How the record is signed or sealed, how its content is fixed by digest and third-party time attestation, and how a later verifier can re-establish that it has not changed.

bundles.name: Time, validity and lifecycle
bundles.description: The distinct times attaching to a decision, the period during which it is valid, its status transitions and finality, and the ways it is superseded, revoked, challenged or annulled.
bundles.rationale: Decision records fail most often on time: a single 'decision date' cannot express that consent became effective when the last consent was delivered, that issuance and service differ, that validity is a range distinct from issuance, or that annulment operates retroactively. RFC 3339, DCMI Terms and Delaware §141(f) each supply primary support for separating these.

layers.name: Temporal frame
layers.description: The set of separately recorded times around a decision, and the validity period distinct from any of them.

findings.name: Decision event timeline
findings.description: The distinct, separately recorded moments in a decision's life — taken, consented, signed, issued, served, published, in force — plus the observation time at which each was recorded.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The timeline is a set of typed timestamp values on the decision record, each already evidenced by an artifact owned elsewhere in the model: proof of service under f25, the time-stamp token under f15 and the event-history entry under f15. Minting a separate timeline artifact would duplicate those without adding evidential weight.

findings.name: Validity window, retroactivity and expiry
findings.description: The period during which the decision is valid, whether effect reaches backwards in time, and how expiry, renewal and suspension of validity are represented.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is a temporal property of the decision expressed inline through a start, an end and suspension intervals. Where an authority issues a separate certificate of validity or currency, that is an outward-facing attestation carried by the notification artifact under f25, not a distinct object owned here.

layers.name: Lifecycle, change and challenge
layers.description: Status transitions and the point of finality, the mechanisms by which a decision is amended, replaced or undone, and the routes by which it can be challenged.

findings.name: Status model and finality
findings.description: The permitted states of a decision record, the transitions between them, and the point at which the decision becomes final and the record unalterable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The status model is a governed enumeration and transition table applied to the record, with each transition already evidenced by the immutable event-history artifact defined under f15. Duplicating that evidence as a second artifact would create two competing audit trails.

findings.name: Supersession, amendment, corrigendum and revocation
findings.description: How a later act changes or displaces this decision, distinguishing correction of the text from amendment of the substance and from withdrawal of the decision itself.

findings.name: Challenge, appeal, review and annulment
findings.description: The routes by which the decision can be contested, the time limits and suspensive effects that apply, and how the outcome of a challenge is recorded against the original.

findings.name: Adjudicative grade and conclusiveness
findings.description: In hearings under APA § 557, a presiding employee may issue an initial decision that becomes the agency decision unless appealed or reviewed; otherwise a recommended or tentative decision may be required, except where the agency finds on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably requires omission.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Grade and conclusiveness are legal-state fields of the record. The supporting finding of imperative omission, if any, is text on this record rather than a new artefact type.

bundles.name: Relational context
bundles.description: The links that place a decision in its wider setting — the matter, occasion and prior decisions that produced it, and the parties and objects it acts upon.
bundles.rationale: A decision record with no outward links cannot be audited, aggregated or enforced. PROV-O supplies the generic derivation and association links, ECLI's metadata expectations imply citation links between decisions, and the registry's own CONTAINS and COMPOSE relations to the meeting and administrative-case models require explicit linkage semantics on this side.

layers.name: Contextual linkage
layers.description: Typed relationships from the decision to its procedural context, related decisions, addressees and subject objects.

findings.name: Relationships to matter, occasion and other decisions
findings.description: Typed links to the case or matter, the meeting or consent process that produced the decision, and prior, related, implementing and cited decisions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are typed references to objects owned by other models — the meeting by WM-ACT-025, the case by WM-POL-017, and other decisions by further instances of this model. Materialising them as an artifact would create a second, divergent copy of relationships that the referenced models already hold authoritatively.

findings.name: Addressees, affected parties and subject objects
findings.description: Who the decision is addressed to, who else it affects, and which concrete objects — assets, applications, permits, budgets, systems — it operates on.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Addressees and subject objects are references into party, asset and application models that own their master data. This finding governs only the linkage and the effect characterisation; holding a local artifact would duplicate party master data and create an unmanaged personal-data copy.

findings.name: Generating activity, used entities and derivation
findings.description: A decision record is a PROV entity generated by a deciding activity that used submissions, evidence, prior decisions, models or meeting records. Derivation and revision relate a later record to an earlier one without implying that usage alone is sufficient. Bundles support provenance of provenance.

bundles.name: Automated and assisted decisioning
bundles.description: How much of the decision was made by a machine, which system and configuration produced it, and what human oversight, explanation and contestability attach as a result.
bundles.rationale: Where a decision is taken wholly or partly by a system, additional and legally consequential context becomes mandatory: the system's identity and version, the logic applied, human oversight, and the affected person's right to intervention, to express a point of view and to contest. GDPR Article 22, the Article 29 Working Party guidance and the AI Act's oversight and logging duties all attach to this distinction, and XACML supplies the structure of a machine-rendered decision result.

layers.name: Automation, oversight and explanation
layers.description: Decision mode and system attribution, and the oversight, explanation and contest mechanisms triggered by automation.

findings.name: Decision mode and system attribution
findings.description: Whether the decision was human, system-assisted or solely automated, and which system, model, policy version and inputs produced or shaped the result.

findings.name: Human oversight, explanation and contestability
findings.description: The oversight measures applied to an automated or assisted decision, the explanation owed to the affected person, and the mechanisms for intervention and contest.

bundles.name: Disclosure, retention and interoperability
bundles.description: How the decision is published or served, who may access which parts under what redactions, how long it is kept and how it is disposed of, and how it is expressed for exchange with external systems.
bundles.rationale: A decision that is not communicated may not take effect, and one that is over-disclosed breaches confidentiality and personal-data duties. Charter Article 41(2)(b) grants file access subject to confidentiality; NARA's ERM requirements and MoReq2010 supply disposal, transfer and hold mechanics; ECLI, Akoma Ntoso, DCMI and PROV supply the exchange vocabularies.

layers.name: Disclosure, notification and access
layers.description: Proactive publication and individual service, access classification, redaction and anonymisation.

findings.name: Publication, notification and service
findings.description: How the decision is made known — published to a register or the public, and served on or notified to addressees — and the proof that communication occurred.

findings.name: Access classification, confidentiality and redaction
findings.description: Who may see which parts of the record, what must be withheld or anonymised, and how a party's right to access their own file is reconciled with confidentiality.

layers.name: Retention, disposition and external alignment
layers.description: How long the decision record is kept and how it is disposed of or transferred, and how it is projected into external identifier schemes and vocabularies.

findings.name: Retention trigger, disposition and disposal hold
findings.description: The event that starts the retention clock for a decision, the authorised disposition outcome, and the holds that suspend disposal.

findings.name: External alignment, identifiers and exchange projection
findings.description: How the decision record maps to external identifier schemes and vocabularies for exchange, and which mappings are lossy, conflicting or unsupported.

model.name: Employment
model.purpose: Represent one governed, jurisdiction-qualified employment relationship between a worker party and an employing party, including identity, classification evidence, terms, assignment realization, continuity, separation, disagreement and provenance without depending on storage or interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns employment relationship identity, party-role topology, asserted basis and jurisdiction, purpose-qualified classification assertions and determinations, effective term bindings, assignment realization links, relationship state, continuity and separation events, party assertions, evidence quality, privacy and interoperability projections while external systems own parties, positions, assignments, occupations, contracts, payroll, attendance, benefits, tax, social insurance, qualifications, recruitment, access grants and evidence objects.
in_scope: Employment relationship identity, worker and employing-party bindings, multi-party roles, basis, jurisdiction, classification assertions, determinations and recognition indicators
Commencement, probation, term bindings, working-time and workplace context, position, assignment, occupation and skill references
Relationship state, continuity, interruption, succession, separation, disputes, evidence, privacy, retention, verification, provenance and exchange
out_of_scope: Generic organizational membership and affiliation, which belong to WM-ORG-006 Membership

Person, organization, unit, position, occupation, assignment, contract, payroll, compensation, attendance, benefits, tax, social insurance, qualification, recruitment, performance and work-product master lifecycles
A universal legal definition of employee, worker or self-employment, or automatic authority for an agent to determine status, change terms, disclose sensitive data or end employment

boundary_notes.distinction: Employment is a work relationship with asserted legal or factual basis, terms and labour effects; generic belonging, affiliation and member standing are owned by WM-ORG-006.
WM-ORG-016 owns assignment identity, scope, duties, execution and lifecycle; Employment owns only the typed, time-qualified link showing which assignments realize the relationship.
A position can exist vacant, a role is a reusable concept and an occupation classifies similar jobs; none is an employment relationship or proves its legal status.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Contract, Policy, Law and Collective Agreement
boundary_notes.distinction: Normative instruments retain independent identity, text, authority, version and lifecycle; Employment stores versioned applicability and precedence bindings.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Payroll, Compensation, Attendance, Benefits, Tax and Social Insurance
boundary_notes.distinction: Transactions and accounts remain external evidence or consequences; their existence or absence alone never proves relationship identity, status or continuity.
Candidate selection and operational onboarding or offboarding are processes that may create or implement employment but do not own the relationship's continuing legal and evidential record.

functions.name: Register employment
functions.description: Create or attest one employment relationship with stable identity, party bindings, asserted basis and explicit unknowns.
preconditions: actor has register or attest authority
duplicate check completed
effects: new relationship identity and provenance are recorded

functions.name: Assert or determine status
functions.description: Record a purpose-qualified party assertion, statistical classification or competent legal determination without collapsing them.
preconditions: scheme, purpose and jurisdiction are pinned
effects: parallel status views remain attributable and queryable

functions.name: Bind term version
functions.description: Attach a versioned external term source with precedence, validity and party acknowledgement.
preconditions: term source is resolvable
authority and effective time are known
effects: prior binding remains preserved and the active view is recomputed

functions.name: Link assignment realization
functions.description: Link a WM-ORG-016 assignment that realizes the relationship without importing assignment execution.
preconditions: identities and non-overlap policy validate
effects: assignment becomes discoverable from employment while retaining external mastership

functions.name: Record commencement
functions.description: Append agreed, actual and effective start facts plus probation and credited-service references.
preconditions: relationship exists
times and sources are qualified
effects: relationship lifecycle begins without overwriting antecedent evidence

functions.name: Suspend or resume
functions.description: Record relationship-level effect of leave, suspension, secondment or resumption.
preconditions: authority and current state permit transition
effects: continuity, affected clocks and assignments are explicitly qualified

functions.name: Record employer succession
functions.description: Create a predecessor or successor employer binding with a continuity decision and changed-term map.
preconditions: party identities are distinct
continuity basis is cited
effects: relationship history remains continuous or explicitly closes and succeeds

functions.name: Amend relationship
functions.description: Append an authorized relationship revision and preserve party acknowledgements and disagreement.
preconditions: change scope and effective time are valid
effects: prior revision remains citable and contested fields stay visible

functions.name: Record separation
functions.description: Record end basis, notice, reason, effective time, challenge state and surviving references.
preconditions: actor authority and applicable profile validate
effects: relationship enters ended or disputed-end state without cascading deletion

functions.name: Reconcile assertions
functions.description: Compare party and authority assertions and append agreement, disagreement or unresolved reconciliation.
preconditions: sources and authority scopes are known
effects: no source is silently overwritten and conflict remains queryable

functions.name: Issue minimal verification
functions.description: Create a purpose-bound projection of necessary employment facts under consent or legal authority.
preconditions: identity, authority and minimum-necessary fields validate
effects: disclosure is attributable, scoped, expiring and auditable

functions.name: Project employment profile
functions.description: Transform a validated revision into a pinned statistical, HR or linked-data profile with declared loss.
preconditions: source and target versions are pinned
effects: mapping lineage, omissions and round-trip limits are recorded

composition.purpose: Represent assignments as typed external realizations of employment without importing their execution or lifecycle.

composition.target: Person, Organization, Organizational Unit, Position, Occupation, Skill, Contract, Policy, Payroll, Benefit, Tax, Social Insurance, Qualification, Evidence and Access models
composition.purpose: Connect governed employment context while retaining source ownership and independent lifecycle.
Qualify employment-recognition indicators, disguised relationships, party labels, determination and dispute principles.
Project statistical status and occupation classifications without granting them universal legal effect.
Reference versioned multilingual occupation and skill concepts.
Project qualified organization relationships, roles, intervals, assertions, derivation and revision while excluding generic membership from the Employment boundary.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, employment-record steward, worker-rights authority and namespace
Person, organization, position, assignment, occupation, contract, policy, payroll, evidence, access and lifecycle-event registries
Master-system mappings for worker, employer, relationship, assignment, status determination and authoritative instrument identifiers
Jurisdiction, classification, privacy, correction, retention, federation and autonomous-agent policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint employment relationship and assertion identifiers in the adopting Dimension namespace only when no authoritative master identifier exists; preserve parties, assignments, occupations, contracts, payroll, benefits, instruments, evidence and decisions as typed references.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
Dimension-local employment, relationship-assertion, status-determination, access and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative employment relationship identifier, issuer and master system, never by worker-employer pair, contract number, position, payroll account, start date or hash alone.
Keep employment, membership, assignment, position, occupation, contract, payroll, attendance, benefit, tax, social-insurance and evidence lifecycles distinct.
patch_rules: Additive extensions declare target bundle, layer or finding, jurisdiction and worker category, source, authority, privacy, rights and interoperability impact.
Identity, party-role, status-effect or lifecycle-semantics changes require a successor version, bitemporal migration map, rollback path and continued resolution of prior records.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when relationship identity, party roles, classification scope, valid time, authority, disagreement, access and lifecycle meaning remain intact.
Statistical, HR, legal and linked-data projections pin source and target versions and disclose transformed, omitted, aggregated or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative employment master-system identifier qualified by issuer and relationship namespace.
Governed globally resolvable employment relationship IRI with explicit worker and employing-party references.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep asserted, agreed, effective, observed, decision, knowledge, notice and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {employment-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use a person's name, employer name, date, job title, contract number, filename or hash alone as relationship identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and profile versions, authority, valid and knowledge times, provenance, assurance, licence and access marking for every retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may attest, register, classify, determine, amend, suspend, transfer, separate, verify, disclose, correct, retain and tombstone employment records.
Employment status is jurisdiction-bound: statistical categories, contract labels, payroll entries and operational indicators are evidence, not universally dispositive legal conclusions.
The worker-employer relationship is power-asymmetric; bilateral provenance never grants either party unilateral authority to erase the other's lawful record, block access or suppress a dispute.

Persons, organizations, positions, assignments, occupations, contracts, payroll, attendance, benefits, tax, social insurance, qualifications, recruitment and work products remain in their owning systems and are referenced.

Automated agents may read, validate, reconcile and append low-risk observations within policy; legal-status determinations, adverse changes, wider disclosure, separation and destructive retirement require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, jurisdiction profile, requested valid and knowledge time, evidence freshness and access scope; return the minimum permitted projection with disputed and unknown fields intact.
create: Create stable relationship identity, worker and employing-party references, asserted basis, jurisdiction, source provenance and explicit unknowns before attaching terms or assignments.
update: Append an assertion, event or successor revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 time, evidence and before-and-after validation; never overwrite a cited assertion, determination or event.
delete: Apply worker-rights, legal-hold, dispute, payroll, tax, social-insurance and retention policy; prefer end state or tombstone, preserve identity and history, and never cascade into referenced parties, assignments, contracts, payments or evidence.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Own namespace, mastership, delegation, access, retention and federation rules.

roles.name: Worker or worker-authorized steward
responsibilities: Attest worker-side facts, exercise access and correction rights, acknowledge changes and preserve contested assertions.

roles.name: Employer or employing authority
responsibilities: Attest employer-side basis, terms, status events and statutory records within mandate.

roles.name: HR or relationship registrar
responsibilities: Maintain identifiers, party bindings, effective terms, assignment links and lifecycle records without making unauthorized legal conclusions.

roles.name: Competent status or labour authority
responsibilities: Determine status, scope, effective period, remedy and appeal effect within jurisdiction.

roles.name: Worker representative or collective-bargaining steward
responsibilities: Maintain representative authority and collective-instrument bindings and support dispute evidence.

roles.name: Privacy and access steward
responsibilities: Apply purpose limitation, minimum disclosure, access, correction, portability, retention and security rules.

roles.name: Independent auditor
responsibilities: Review authority, changes, disclosures, corrections and provenance without rewriting party evidence.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and disclosure of person-linked terms, compensation, health, dispute, separation or performance-related data unless active Dimension, role, purpose, jurisdiction and field policy grant it; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Statutory, judicial, labour-inspection or emergency access must cite authority, be purpose-bound, attributable and reviewable, and must not erase original assertions, disputes, decisions or audit evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, relationship and party identities, action, policy and jurisdiction profile, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected scope, requested and effective authority, evidence and outcome.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, employment mastership, worker-rights, jurisdiction, privacy, correction, retention, dispute and federation policies.

Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required person, organization, assignment, position, occupation, contract, policy, payroll, evidence, access and decision model instructions before mutation or disclosure.

coverage.claim: A source-grounded reviewable draft of one governed Employment relationship across ILO employment-relationship, work-status and occupation standards, selected EU working-condition, agency-work and privacy profiles, W3C organizational and provenance patterns, and RFC 3339 time, without a claim of universal legal-status, jurisdiction, labour-category, HR-schema or certified crosswalk completeness.

checklist.notes: Stable relationship identity, issuer, aliases, duplicates and successor lineage are explicit.
Employment is separated from membership, assignment and self-employment while jurisdiction and purpose qualify status.
Party topology, basis, terms, capacity and relationship-owned state are represented; physical properties are not applicable.
Indicators, counter-indicators, methods, determination authority, confidence and confusing neighboring classes are covered.
Register, classify, bind, link, amend, suspend, transfer, separate, reconcile, verify and project operations are governed.
Assignments realize employment through a typed candidate relation while all neighboring master lifecycles remain external.
Commencement, probation, continuity, interruption, succession, amendment and separation retain immutable history.
Worker, employer, agency, host, client, paymaster, platform, authority, assignment and instrument roles are typed and time-qualified.
Asserted, agreed, effective, observed, decision, notice and knowledge times remain distinct and use RFC 3339 for events.
Workplace, remote, mobile, host-territory and cross-border context are referenced with jurisdiction implications.
Party and authority assertions, evidence, derivation, revision and reconciliation are attributable.
Bilateral evidence and power asymmetry are explicit; each referenced record retains its master system.
Duplicates, status scope, indicator sufficiency, stale state, conflicting assertions and projection loss are checked.
Purpose limitation, minimum disclosure, correction, restriction, worker access and audit are covered.
Per-field retention, legal hold, tombstone and non-cascading deletion preserve lawful evidence and history.
ICSE, ISCO, ESCO, W3C ORG, HR and jurisdiction profiles are pinned and loss-aware.

known_omissions: National and subnational labour-law, public-service, military, seafarer, domestic-work, child-work, platform-work, apprenticeship and collective-bargaining profiles require specialist treatment.
Contract, assignment, payroll, compensation, benefits, attendance, leave, tax, social insurance, qualification, recruitment and performance lifecycles remain in neighboring models.
Certified HR-schema, ICSE-18, ISCO-08, ESCO and jurisdictional crosswalks, conformance suites and rights-impact fixtures remain future work.
conflicts: Employment status may differ between statistical, tax, social-insurance and labour-law purposes and must never be collapsed into one unqualified category.
The employer, agency, host, client, paymaster, platform and beneficial controller may differ in multi-party work.
An assignment, payroll event, workplace credential or contract label may exist without proving current employment status or legal effect.
regional_assumptions: EU Directives 2019/1152 and 2008/104/EC and the GDPR provide European profiles and do not create universal global legal obligations.
ILO Convention No. 158 is applicable only where its ratification and implementation scope is verified; Recommendation No. 198 remains guidance for national policy.
ICSE-18 and ISCO-08 are statistical classifications and ESCO is a European semantic classification, not direct legal-status authorities.
adversarial_checks: Reject any Employment record that includes generic organizational membership or treats worker-employer pair, job title, contract number or payroll account as unique identity.
Reject a legal-status conclusion inferred solely from party label, contract type, payment method, occupation, one control indicator or ICSE category.
Reject ownership inferred from record custody and reject employer-only control over worker access, correction, dispute, portability or lawful retention.
Reject active-status inference from an assignment, payroll event, building access or old contract without qualified current evidence.
Reject mutation, verification or separation beyond the actor's jurisdiction, purpose, field scope and authority and preserve prior assertions bitemporally.

boundaryDecision.status: accepted as a jurisdiction-qualified employment relationship
boundaryDecision.rationale: The model represents one work relationship between a worker party and an employing party. Membership, parties, positions, assignments, occupations, contracts, payroll, attendance, benefits, tax, social insurance, qualifications, recruitment and evidence remain distinct linked records or objects.

decisions.rationale: The current registry explicitly requires Employment to exclude generic belonging and affiliation, which are owned by WM-ORG-006 Membership.

A worker-employer pair may have several concurrent or successive relationships, so neither party pair, job title, assignment, contract number, payroll account, start date nor hash is sufficient identity.

decisions.disposition: accepted as purpose-qualified and jurisdiction-qualified assertions
decisions.rationale: Statistical, tax, social-insurance and labour-law status may differ, while ILO Recommendation No. 198 makes facts and national determination mechanisms more important than party labels.
ICSE-18 organizes jobs by authority and economic risk and helps recognize employees and dependent contractors, but it does not itself create universal legal status.
Employer, agency, host, client, paymaster, platform and competent authority may differ, especially for temporary-agency, dispatched and platform-mediated work.
WM-ORG-016 owns assignment identity, scope, execution and lifecycle. Employment owns only the typed interval-qualified link showing that an assignment realizes the relationship.
ISCO-08 distinguishes a concrete job from an occupation class, and W3C ORG distinguishes posts and roles from qualified person-organization relationships.

Contracts, collective agreements, policies, payroll, attendance, benefits, tax and social-insurance records keep their own masters and lifecycles; Employment records applicability, precedence and evidential links.
A competent determination may be retroactive, but it must not erase what parties or systems previously asserted or when the determination became known.

decisions.disposition: accepted as multi-party provenance, not unilateral ownership
decisions.rationale: Both parties may contribute and hold evidence, but neither party automatically controls the other's lawful access, correction, portability, dispute record or retention duties.
Assignments, payroll events, workplace access and old contracts may be evidence but never alone establish current employment, suspension, continuity or separation.
The relation ledger contains a candidate WM-ORG-005 COMPOSE WM-ORG-016 row, not an approved relation, so the proposed assignment-realization link remains draft.

The relation ledger marks WM-ORG-005 COMPOSE WM-ORG-016 as candidate rather than approved, and other neighboring model relations are not approved, so all proposed composition remains draft.

bundles.name: Relationship identity, parties and authority
bundles.description: Identifies the employment relationship and the parties and authorities around it.
bundles.rationale: A relationship must remain resolvable independently of mutable jobs, assignments, labels and organizations' internal records.

layers.name: Relationship master identity
layers.description: Stable identity, aliases, source systems and duplicate or successor handling.

findings.name: Authoritative relationship identifier and master system
findings.description: The stable identifier, issuer, namespace, master system, status and typed aliases for one employment relationship.

findings.name: Duplicate, merge, split, transfer and successor lineage
findings.description: Rules and evidence that reconcile duplicates or create successors without erasing cited relationship identities.

layers.name: Party topology and authority
layers.description: Worker, employer and other party roles, their effective intervals and authority sources.

findings.name: Worker and employing party bindings
findings.description: Typed references to worker and employing party with asserted and effective role intervals and identity provenance.

findings.name: Agency, host, client, paymaster, platform and authority roles
findings.description: Allows multi-party work without treating every operational or payment party as the legal employer.

bundles.name: Legal classification, jurisdiction and recognition
bundles.description: Separates evidence, statistical classifications, party assertions and legally effective determinations.
bundles.rationale: Employment status is jurisdiction-bound and may be disputed, retroactively determined or different for different purposes.

layers.name: Basis, jurisdiction and instruments
layers.description: The asserted basis, applicable territory, purpose and governing instruments.

findings.name: Contractual, statutory, factual and appointment basis
findings.description: References the instrument or facts said to create employment and records who asserts that basis.

findings.name: Jurisdiction, scope, applicable law and collective instruments
findings.description: Pins territorial, personal and subject scope plus applicable legal, collective, policy and ratification profiles.

layers.name: Status classification and indicators
layers.description: Records purpose-qualified categories and the evidence used for them.

findings.name: Employee, worker, dependent-contractor and self-employed assertions
findings.description: Parallel party, statistical, administrative and legal status assertions with scheme, purpose, time and confidence.

findings.name: Control, dependence, remuneration, risk and integration indicators
findings.description: Observable indicators and counter-indicators with method, source and applicability, never a label-only conclusion.

layers.name: Determination, dispute and recognition
layers.description: Recognition criteria, competent determinations, competing assertions and correction.

findings.name: Competent status determination, scope and effect
findings.description: Authority, decision reference, legal basis, effective period, appeal state and exact purposes for which a determination controls.

findings.name: Misclassification dispute, appeal and retroactive correction
findings.description: Contested status, claims, decisions, remedies and bitemporal corrections while prior assertions remain visible.

bundles.name: Commencement, terms and working context
bundles.description: Captures when the relationship begins and which external terms and work-context assertions apply.
bundles.rationale: Transparent working conditions require versioned, time-qualified bindings rather than copied contract or payroll payloads.

layers.name: Commencement, probation and time
layers.description: Agreed, recorded, effective and recognized beginning and probation facts.

findings.name: Agreement, appointment, start and antecedent service
findings.description: Creation basis, agreed and actual start, credited prior service, seniority anchor and evidence references.

findings.name: Probation, trial, confirmation and rescission
findings.description: Probation basis, limits, extensions, outcome and relationship effect without confusing probation with employment identity.

layers.name: Term bindings and precedence
layers.description: Versioned references to individual, collective, statutory and policy terms.

findings.name: Duration, renewal, notice and precedence
findings.description: Open-ended or fixed duration, end condition, renewal, notice method and precedence among applicable term sources.

findings.name: Remuneration, benefit, training and expense references
findings.description: Bindings to compensation, benefit, training and reimbursable-expense masters with effective time and disclosure class.

layers.name: Working time, place and pattern
layers.description: Capacity and location context that qualifies the relationship without replacing schedules or attendance.

findings.name: Capacity, working-time pattern, overtime and predictability
findings.description: Contracted capacity, standard pattern, predictability, reference hours and applicable overtime or minimum-notice rules.

findings.name: Workplace, remote, mobile and cross-border context
findings.description: Primary and permitted places, remote or mobile mode, host territory, travel expectation and jurisdiction implications by reference.

bundles.name: Role, assignment and occupation binding
bundles.description: Connects employment to positions, assignments, occupations and skills without importing their lifecycles.
bundles.rationale: A relationship can continue through several jobs or assignments, and an occupation is a classifier rather than the relationship itself.

layers.name: Position, role and assignment
layers.description: Time-qualified realization links to externally mastered organizational work records.

findings.name: Position, unit, role and reporting references
findings.description: References formal positions, organizational units, role concepts and reporting structures without copying them into employment.

findings.name: Assignment realization, validity and concurrency
findings.description: Links one employment relationship to concurrent or sequential WM-ORG-016 assignments and records link validity only.

layers.name: Job, occupation and skill context
layers.description: Separates the concrete job from reusable occupation and skill concepts.

findings.name: Job, task, duty and occupation-classification reference
findings.description: Binds current or historic job and assignment references to versioned ISCO, ESCO or local occupation concepts.

findings.name: Required, used and developed skill references
findings.description: Purpose-qualified links to skill concepts and evidence while qualifications and assessments remain external.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, continuity and separation
bundles.description: Represents relationship state and change independently of assignment, payroll or access-system activity.
bundles.rationale: Employment may continue through leave, transfer or employer succession and may end through several governed bases, so changes need explicit effect and authority.

layers.name: Status, continuity and succession
layers.description: Current and historic relationship state, continuity and successor employer bindings.

findings.name: Active, inactive, disputed and unknown relationship state
findings.description: Time-qualified state assertion, source, confidence and validation that never derives state from one operational system alone.

findings.name: Employer succession, transfer and service continuity
findings.description: Predecessor and successor parties, authority, continuity decision, credited service and unchanged or changed term bindings.

layers.name: Interruption, change and resumption
layers.description: Relationship-level effects of leave, suspension, secondment and material amendment.

findings.name: Leave, suspension, secondment and nonperformance effect
findings.description: References the external event and records whether employment, service, pay, benefits, assignment and notice clocks continue or pause.

findings.name: Term amendment, consent, authority and effective change
findings.description: The proposed and effective change, source instrument, affected bindings, party acknowledgements and dispute state.

layers.name: Separation and post-employment
layers.description: End basis, procedure, contest and surviving bindings.

findings.name: Resignation, expiry, dismissal, mutual end and other basis
findings.description: Qualified separation basis, initiating party, decision or notice references, stated reason, effective time and uncertainty.

findings.name: Notice, challenge, remedy and surviving-obligation references
findings.description: Notice compliance, appeal, reinstatement or compensation outcome and surviving confidentiality or other obligation bindings.

bundles.name: Assertions, evidence, privacy and trust
bundles.description: Keeps both parties' assertions, authoritative determinations and minimum-disclosure access auditable.
bundles.rationale: Employment data is sensitive and power-asymmetric; provenance and access rights cannot be collapsed into employer ownership of the truth.

layers.name: Party assertions, evidence and quality
layers.description: Attribution, acknowledgement, discrepancies and evidence quality for relationship facts.

findings.name: Worker, employer, third-party and authority assertions
findings.description: Parallel attributable statements with purpose, valid time, knowledge time, confidence, acknowledgement and contest status.

findings.name: Evidence, attestation, freshness, quality and reconciliation
findings.description: Evidence references, issuer, collection method, freshness, reliability, conflicts and explicit reconciliation outcome.

layers.name: Privacy, access, retention and verification
layers.description: Purpose-bound access, correction, retention and minimum employment verification.

findings.name: Purpose, access, correction, portability and restriction
findings.description: Field and artifact access by role and purpose, worker access, correction route, portability profile and lawful restrictions.

findings.name: Retention, deletion, legal hold and minimal verification
findings.description: Per-field retention and tombstone rules plus consent or authority bound verification of only necessary relationship facts.

bundles.name: Interoperability, governance and agent operations
bundles.description: Controls profiles, projections, autonomous checks and safe relationship change.
bundles.rationale: Machine exchange must preserve authority, time, disagreement, privacy and information-loss semantics across HR, statistical and linked-data projections.

layers.name: Profiles, projections and agent control
layers.description: Versioned mappings and permissioned agent actions.

findings.name: Jurisdiction, statistical, HR and linked-data profiles
findings.description: Pinned source and target versions, mapping scope, transformed or omitted values, validation and non-round-trip declarations.

findings.name: Agent operation authority, validation and audit
findings.description: Allowed read, append, reconcile, propose, confirm and forbidden actions with preconditions, effects, rollback and audit evidence.

model.name: Payroll / Compensation
model.purpose: Represent payroll runs and independently governed payee compensation results so agents can understand how terms and source evidence become earnings, bases, deductions, contributions, net pay, payment instructions, statements and reports without confusing calculation with approval, settlement, filing acceptance or accounting posting.
model.scope_statement: Owns payroll-run, payee-result and revision identities; regular, supplemental, off-cycle, final, advance, retroactive, correction, reversal and void classes; employer, worker, engagement, job, position, pay-group, administrator, approver and authority bindings; earning, pay, tax, cutoff and payday periods; jurisdiction, establishment, work-location, currency and calendar profiles; salary, wage, rate, unit, overtime, commission, bonus, allowance, reimbursement, in-kind, benefit and employer-contribution terms; source-qualified time, leave, absence, expense, sales, performance, election, eligibility, proration and override inputs; earning components, gross earnings, taxable, pensionable, insurable, minimum-wage and overtime bases; statutory, voluntary, tax, social insurance, pension, benefit, union, garnishment, loan and other deductions; employer contributions, net pay, employer cost, rounding, balancing and accumulators; payment allocation, instruction, execution, rejection, return, recall, settlement and reconciliation references; pay-statement and filing projections, delivery, receipt, submission, authority-response and correction evidence; run controls, validation, approval, release, retroactivity, reversal and reconciliation; rule versions, intermediate results, derivation, quality, clocks, privacy, access, retention and loss-aware projections. External worker, engagement, organization, job, timekeeping, leave, expense, sales, performance, benefit, tax, payment, bank account, ledger, filing, dispute and records masters remain authoritative.
in_scope: Payroll-run and payee-result identity, parties, periods, jurisdiction and compensation profiles, source inputs, terms, components, calculations, bases, deductions, contributions, net pay and employer cost
Payment, statement, filing and remittance bindings, lifecycle controls, corrections, reconciliation, clocks, provenance, privacy, access, retention, validation and projections
out_of_scope: Owning Person, Worker, Engagement, Organization, Job, Position, Timekeeping, Leave, Expense, Sales, Performance, Benefit Plan, Tax Account, Court Order, Bank Account, Payment, Accounting Ledger, Filing, Dispute or Records masters
Treating compensation term as earned pay, gross as taxable base, net pay as payment, issued statement as receipt, submitted filing as authority acceptance, or correction as deletion
Autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, protected-data disclosure or record destruction

boundary_notes.distinction: The unified registry supplies WM-ORG-005 as a provisional parent signal only. Organization and employment governance remain external and no settled containment edge exists.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Payroll run versus payee compensation result
boundary_notes.distinction: A run groups calculation and control context; each payee result has its own worker binding, components, values, states, access and correction lineage.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Compensation terms, inputs, calculated result and payment
boundary_notes.distinction: Terms authorize possible remuneration, source records evidence activity or eligibility, calculation derives values and payment systems execute instructions; none proves another.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Tax, benefit, filing, remittance and accounting records
boundary_notes.distinction: Payroll binds source-qualified external records and rule profiles; calculated or filed values never prove authority acceptance, remittance settlement, benefit delivery or ledger posting.
Each labour, tax, reporting, payment, statistical, privacy or schema source covers a scoped profile; every mapping is version-pinned and loss-declaring.

functions.name: Initialize payroll run
functions.description: Governed operation to initialize payroll run without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
inputs: employer, pay group and run class
preconditions: namespace, periods, employer authority, pay group, calendar and jurisdiction profiles are resolved
effects: creates a draft run only and does not create worker, engagement, time, payment, tax, filing or ledger masters

functions.name: Bind payee result
functions.description: Governed operation to bind payee result without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: worker reference, engagement, pay group, jurisdiction and access basis are resolved
effects: adds a payee result without copying protected worker or contract masters

functions.name: Ingest source inputs
functions.description: Governed operation to ingest source inputs without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
inputs: time, leave, expense, sales, performance or election evidence
preconditions: source identity, period, authority, approval, freshness and correction lineage are known
effects: records source-qualified inputs and never treats an input as earned, approved or payable by itself

functions.name: Evaluate compensation rules
functions.description: Governed operation to evaluate compensation rules without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
outputs: eligible components, rates, bases and rule trace
preconditions: all rule, table, formula, agreement and jurisdiction versions are pinned
effects: evaluates eligibility and calculations reproducibly without amending source agreements or laws

functions.name: Calculate pay result
functions.description: Governed operation to calculate pay result without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
outputs: gross, bases, deductions, contributions, net pay and employer-cost assertions
preconditions: calculation inputs, intermediate results, accumulators and precision policy are present
effects: creates a calculated result that does not prove approval, payment, settlement, filing or posting

functions.name: Validate and balance
functions.description: Governed operation to validate and balance without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
outputs: validation findings, balance evidence and review queue
preconditions: minimum wage, overtime, base, deduction, priority, threshold, ceiling, rounding and control rules are resolvable
effects: records pass, fail, warning or exception evidence without silently overriding values

functions.name: Approve and release
functions.description: Governed operation to approve and release without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
preconditions: delegated authority, segregation, review, exceptions, digest and cutoff lock are satisfied
effects: changes lifecycle state but never executes payment, remittance, filing or ledger posting

functions.name: Project statements, payments and filings
functions.description: Governed operation to project statements, payments and filings without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
outputs: statement, payment, remittance and filing projections plus loss declarations
preconditions: destination, authority, privacy, schema, code-set and release versions are pinned
effects: creates external instructions or reports only; their execution, delivery, receipt and acceptance remain external events

functions.name: Correct, reverse and reconcile
functions.description: Governed operation to correct, reverse and reconcile without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
inputs: external payment, filing and ledger evidence
outputs: successor, reversal, adjustment and reconciliation assertions
preconditions: original facts remain immutable and authority, effective period, impact and downstream obligations are known
effects: preserves lineage and does not infer payment recovery, authority acceptance or ledger correction

functions.name: Validate, project, retain and audit
functions.description: Governed operation to validate, project, retain and audit without autonomous compensation change, calculation override, approval, payment, filing, disclosure or destruction.
outputs: validation report, minimum view, loss declaration, retention result or audit event
preconditions: schema, currency, rule, digest, authority, privacy, legal-hold, clock and conformance checks pass
effects: never exposes unnecessary payroll data or cascades deletion into worker, payment, tax, filing, ledger or records masters

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize a payroll run by authoritative employer payroll identifier, pay group, run class, pay date, earning or pay periods and revision head, never by worker name, amount, filename or digest alone.
Canonicalize each payee result separately from the run and keep compensation terms, inputs, calculated results, payment instructions, statements, filings and ledger entries distinct.
patch_rules: Extensions declare worker class, jurisdiction, compensation component, basis, deduction, contribution, accumulator, payment, statement, filing and interoperability effects.
Accepted calculations are immutable; retroactive adjustment, off-cycle correction, reversal and void create linked successors with reason, authority and downstream impact.
Never silently change worker, engagement, employer, period, jurisdiction, currency, rule version, amount type, source input, authority, privacy marking or external reference.
compatibility_rules: Ignore additive fields only when run and result identity, revision, parties, periods, jurisdictions, rules, values, states, clocks, authority, access and provenance survive.
Every projection pins schema, code-set, classifier, currency and jurisdiction versions and declares loss in calculation, reporting, privacy, lifecycle and authority semantics.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for a payroll run, payee result, employer, tax, payment, filing or records object, qualified by namespace and record kind.
Governed globally resolvable payroll-run, payee-result or artifact IRI.
Dimension UUID or ULID when neither preceding identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; distinguish earning, effective, cutoff, calculation, validation, approval, release, payday, payment, settlement, statement, filing, authority-response, correction, observation, ingestion and knowledge times whenever they differ.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, payroll-run and payee-result IDs, revision, actor, purpose, source, rule and policy versions, amount type, currency, unit, precision, event and knowledge times, confidentiality, retention and provenance.

policies: This model owns governed payroll-run and payee-result context, not worker, engagement, organization, job, timekeeping, leave, expense, sales, performance, benefit, tax, payment, ledger, filing, dispute or records masters.

Compensation term, source input, earned amount, gross, statutory base, deduction, employer contribution, net pay, payment instruction, settlement, statement, filing, remittance and ledger posting remain separate assertions.
Jurisdiction, worker classification, labour, tax, social insurance, benefit, garnishment and accounting rules are versioned profiles rather than universal defaults.

Agents cannot autonomously change compensation, waive deductions, override calculation controls, approve a run, move money, file declarations, disclose protected pay data or destroy records without delegated authority.

read: Resolve run, payee result, periods, parties, terms, inputs, rules, components, bases, deductions, contributions, net result, payments, statements, filings, corrections, access and projection loss.
create: Bind employer, run class, pay group, periods, jurisdiction, currency, rule set and initial unknown lifecycle states before calculating any payee result.
update: Append successor inputs, calculations, validations, approvals, payment bindings, statements, filings, authority responses, corrections and reconciliation assertions with reason, authority, source, event time and knowledge time.
delete: Apply labour, tax, privacy, accounting, audit, legal-hold and Dimension retention policy; tombstone only the catalogue view and never cascade deletion to external masters.

known_omissions: Claude and Grok each timed out on one bounded attempt; no independent external result was admitted.
WM-ORG-005 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-031 edge.

Employee, contractor, executive, equity, tips, piecework, commission, bonus, expense, household, domestic, agricultural, seafarer, migrant, public-sector, multi-jurisdiction and multi-currency profiles need separate validation.
Labour, tax, social insurance, pension, benefit, garnishment, privacy, accounting, insolvency and retention rules remain adopting-Dimension profiles.
Every ILO, EU, United States, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, OECD, Eurostat, ISO, XBRL, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL, OWL-Time and OpenAPI mapping needs exact release pins and conformance tests.
conflicts: Payroll run, payee result, compensation agreement, time record, payment, statement, filing, remittance and ledger entry are related but not equivalent identities.
Regular pay, supplemental pay, off-cycle pay, advance, final pay, retroactive adjustment, correction, reversal and void require explicit classes and lineage.
Gross earnings, taxable base, pensionable base, insurable base, deductions, employer contributions, net pay, employer cost and statistical labour cost are distinct axes.
Calculated, validated, approved, released, paid, settled, filed, accepted, reconciled and closed are independent states.
regional_assumptions: Worker classification, wage entitlement, minimum pay, overtime, tax, social insurance, benefits, deductions, garnishments, pay statements, reporting, correction, retention and privacy depend on jurisdiction and engagement.
ILO, EU, United States, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, OECD and Eurostat sources are scoped profiles and not universal payroll law.
adversarial_checks: Reject a payroll record that lacks separate payroll-run and payee-result identities.
Reject a result that absorbs worker, engagement, timekeeping, leave, benefit, tax, payment, ledger, filing or records masters.
Reject an amount without amount type, currency, unit, rule version, source, period, precision and provenance.
Reject net pay as proof of payment instruction, execution, settlement or worker receipt.
Reject filing submission as proof of authority receipt, acceptance, remittance or reconciliation.
Reject destructive correction, silent override or autonomous compensation change, run approval, payment, filing, disclosure or deletion.

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The slash label is resolved as a payroll execution and compensation-result aggregate. It owns payroll runs and independently governed payee calculation results, while compensation plans and agreements, workers, time, benefits, payments, filings and ledgers remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: The model owns calculation and control context, not the full employment or compensation-plan lifecycle. Payroll run and payee result remain separate identities within the aggregate.
The unified registry supplies WM-ORG-005 as a parent hint but the frozen relation ledger has no settled WM-ECO-031 edge, so it grants no containment or cascade authority.
A run groups periods, rules, controls and totals; each result preserves its own worker binding, components, values, states, access and correction lineage.

decisions.concept: Compensation term, source input and calculated value
decisions.rationale: A term defines possible remuneration, an input evidences work or eligibility and a calculation derives values under pinned rules; none silently proves another.

decisions.concept: Regular, supplemental, off-cycle, final, advance, retroactive, correction, reversal and void
decisions.rationale: Each class has different periods, authority, tax treatment, lineage and downstream effects and cannot be inferred from timing or sign alone.

decisions.concept: Gross earnings, statutory bases, deductions, contributions, net pay and employer cost
decisions.rationale: Every value preserves amount type, component, currency, unit, rule version, period, source, precision and derivation and cannot prove another value.

decisions.concept: Calculated, validated, approved, released, paid, settled, filed, accepted, reconciled and closed
decisions.rationale: Calculation and payroll authorization do not prove execution or acceptance by payment, tax, benefit, accounting or reporting systems.

decisions.concept: Payment, statement, filing, remittance and ledger records
decisions.rationale: Payroll may create projections and record returned evidence but does not own bank accounts, payment settlement, authority filings, remittance settlement or accounting postings.

decisions.concept: Retroactive adjustment, correction, reversal and void
decisions.rationale: Corrections preserve the original calculation and source evidence, state the reason and authority and declare downstream payment, filing and ledger impacts.

decisions.concept: Jurisdiction, worker class, labour, tax, benefit and garnishment rules
decisions.rationale: International and national sources define scoped regimes; no rate, threshold, entitlement or deduction rule is universal.
Worker identity, compensation, bank destination, tax, benefit, garnishment, absence and performance facts require purpose-bound least-privilege access and auditable exceptions.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

model.name: Attestation / Credential
model.purpose: Represent issuer-asserted claims with durable identity, evidence, validity, status, securing and purpose-bound presentation while remaining independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns credential class and issued-instance identity, claim and schema references, issuer, subject and holder role bindings, issuance evidence, validity, status and lifecycle, secured representations, credential-specific verification evidence, presentations, disclosure manifests, interoperability mappings and governed retention. Party identity, issuer mandate, subject profile, source evidence, keys, permission-bearing grants, trust policy, authorization decisions and generic audit logs remain external.
in_scope: Credential and attestation definitions, instance and representation identity, typed claims, schema, vocabulary, issuer authority reference, subject binding and issuance evidence
Validity and terms, status method and freshness, suspension, revocation, expiry, renewal, correction, supersession, secured representations and verification results
Presentation requests, disclosures, holder binding, privacy and correlation, format mappings, role views, access, retention, provenance and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person, organization, issuer, subject, holder, verifier, mandate, source evidence, key, trust policy, permit grant, authorization decision or audit-log master lifecycle
Implementing proof, signature, wallet, PKI path, status-list or presentation-protocol algorithms and storing private keys or undisclosed secrets
Universal claim truth, issuer trust, identity proofing, authentication, authorization, eligibility, legal effect or certified cross-format equivalence

boundary_notes.distinction: The credential owns the issuer's claim expression and references evidence; source observations and evidence artifacts keep their own identity and provenance.
Issuer, subject, holder and verifier identities and public key references remain external; credential verification is not authentication by itself.
A licence or permit credential may evidence an external grant, but its authenticity and status do not themselves make an authorization decision.
Generic proof artifacts and verification methods remain external or reusable mixins; this model binds them to credential claim, validity, status and presentation context.
This model records credential-specific presentations and verification evidence, while wallet inventory and generic append-only audit execution remain external.

functions.name: Define credential class and profile
functions.description: Establish claim vocabulary, schema, required evidence, issuer authority, validity, status and representation rules.
preconditions: namespace, semantic definitions, issuer mandate, privacy and interoperability validate
effects: a versioned class is available without issuing an instance

functions.name: Issue attestation or credential
functions.description: Create an immutable issued assertion and representations after an authorized evidence-backed decision.
outputs: issued credential revision and issuance event
preconditions: issuer authority, subject binding, schema, evidence, validity, status method and expected serial validate
effects: issuer record and permitted holder copy are created with provenance

functions.name: Deliver, accept and custody holder copy
functions.description: Transfer a representation to a holder or wallet and record receipt without transferring issuer authority.
preconditions: holder authority, channel, integrity, privacy and recovery policy validate
effects: a controlled copy becomes available to the holder

functions.name: Publish or refresh status
functions.description: Issue a privacy-aware, time-qualified credential status assertion or list update.
preconditions: authority, method, purpose, index, freshness, signing and privacy validate
effects: relying parties can obtain current source-qualified standing

functions.name: Suspend, reinstate, revoke, expire, renew or supersede
functions.description: Append a credential lifecycle event and derived state while preserving earlier claims and representations.
preconditions: transition guard, authority, effective time, status publication, notification and lineage validate
effects: current standing changes without rewriting issued history

functions.name: Create presentation request
functions.description: Record verifier, purpose, audience, requested claims or predicates, formats, nonce and expiry.
preconditions: verifier identity, authority, minimization, client binding, nonce and expiry validate
effects: a bounded disclosure request becomes attributable

functions.name: Derive and present credential
functions.description: Create a request-bound presentation with permitted disclosure and optional holder binding.
preconditions: credential status, request, nonce, audience, holder binding, minimization and format validate
effects: the verifier receives purpose-bound evidence without mutating the credentials

functions.name: Verify credential or presentation
functions.description: Record schema, proof, key, path, status, time and request-binding checks and structured outcome.
preconditions: algorithms, canonicalization, keys, status freshness, time, trust input and policy version validate
effects: technical outcome becomes attributable without making an authorization decision

functions.name: Project or transform loss-aware
functions.description: Map a credential to another representation or sector profile with explicit omissions and semantic conflicts.
preconditions: source and target versions, issuer, subject, claims, validity, proof, status and round-trip class validate
effects: consumer receives a traceable representation with visible limitations

functions.name: Correct, retain, dispose and audit
functions.description: Create a successor correction or execute authorized retention and disposition while preserving required lineage.
preconditions: expected head, issuer authority, legal hold, subject rights, minimum tombstone and post-write checks validate
effects: current data changes without erasing accountable issuance and status history

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint stable IDs for credential classes and issued attestation instances. Preserve authoritative issuer serials and external subject, issuer, key, mandate and evidence identities; never use subject name, date or digest alone.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
